provenance: RECORD-TIER anchor (019 doctrine: deviations are reported, never gated). Full session, method, uncertainty and adjudication record: docs/verification/pool-9ft-measured-calibration.md (audit trail: GitHub issue #5). Anti-overfit doctrine (constitution P-IV): this data legitimizes ONLY the opt-in Measured-tier catalog entries (owner_proam_9ft_2026_07 / owner_proam_cloth_2026_07) and these record-tier anchors; it is NEVER grounds to change global kernel defaults. THE LAYERING IS THE RESULT: cushion restitution separates by ARRIVAL SPIN STATE - pure-roll arrivals rebound at 0.645-0.670 (spin-cushion coupling, consistent with the TP B.6 rolling-arrival anchor ~0.7) while low-spin (still-sliding) arrivals measure e = 0.84-0.94 at 1.4-2.9 m/s, bracketing the kernel constant e_c = 0.85. The v1/v2 'cushion is dead / default 0.2 too high' conclusion is RETRACTED (bake-clock artifact + arrival-spin confounding). title: Cushion restitution - the LAYERED picture (owner's table, v3 definitive, exact pts clock)
reading_guide: There is no single 'e' for this cushion: measured restitution separates by ARRIVAL SPIN STATE and speed. Pure-roll arrivals lose ~35% of speed (spin-cushion coupling eats the rolling component); low-spin (still-sliding) arrivals rebound at 0.84-0.94, bracketing the kernel default e_c = 0.85. This layering is the result - collapsing it to one number reproduces the retracted v1 error.

metadata.e_definitions: B-set e_normal = normal-velocity ratio at near-normal incidence (0.3-2.3 deg); c0-slide e_speed = v_out/v_in scalar ratio at near-normal incidence; A-set e_normal = vn_out/vn_in velocity-component proxy at oblique incidence (spin unmeasured); C-set e_normal = vn_out/vn_in at ~34 deg with slate-labeled follow/draw arrival spin

layers.layer: pure-roll arrival, near-normal incidence, 0.48-0.85 m/s (B tier1)
layers.arrival_spin_state: pure roll, measured: arrival roll ratio 1.02-1.03 (stripe-area FFT)

e_v_slope_per_mps.note: no measurable slope over the 0.48-0.85 m/s span

layers.layer: pure-roll arrival, near-normal incidence, 0.73-0.98 m/s (c0-slide bonus)
layers.arrival_spin_state: pure roll (slide->roll transition at t* = 0.43-0.47 s, contact 1.46-1.86 s after departure); two-phase return fits confirm the cushion returns the ball essentially rolling
layers.note: timeline-free ratio; consistent with B tier1 0.645 +- 0.032 - two independent pipelines

layers.layer: low-spin (sliding / partial-slide) arrivals, 1.4-2.9 m/s: e band 0.84-0.94
layers.arrival_spin_state: still sliding at contact, roll ratio 0.60-0.94 where measured (2 of 10 unmeasured); per-shot annotations below
layers.band_scope: holds for the six shots with v_in 1.42-2.88 m/s (s06 s07 s08 s09 s11 s14); the three fastest tier3 shots (3.09-3.23 m/s) drop to e 0.70-0.79 - see slope entry

tier3_e_v_slope_per_mps.note: first hint of a high-speed knee (~2.9-3.0 m/s sink-in) but arrival spin 0.32-0.70 is a confound; NOT attributable to pure e(v); n=5, unproven

layers.layer: oblique incidence e_n proxies by cell (A matrix; arrival spin UNMEASURED, english cells protocol-labeled)
layers.arrival_spin_state: unmeasured for all cells; 'run'/'rev' = ~0.4R tip-offset protocol labels; e_n is a velocity-component proxy (vn_out/vn_in), not a spin-decomposed restitution
layers.speed_trend: e_n proxy rises with speed at both angles (30 deg none: 0.529 slow -> 0.700 fast; 50 deg none: 0.562 -> 0.710)

layers.layer: C-set follow vs draw at first contact (left cushion, ~34 deg incidence): spin-cushion coupling
layers.arrival_spin_state: follow = topspin arrival, draw = backspin arrival; spin SIGN from slate labels (stripe period gives |omega| only); pre-contact |omega| readable on mid-speed shots, washed out above ~2.5 m/s

post_contact_overspin.systematic: +-20% band-geometry/harmonic systematic on ABSOLUTE spin ratios; the >1 overspin signature is robust, its magnitude is not precise

kernel_context.e_c_retraction: pool-core default e_c = 0.85 constant (params.rs): v3 places low-spin arrivals at 0.84-0.94 (1.4-2.9 m/s) -- the 0.85 default is IN BAND, and v1's 'default is ~0.2 too high' conclusion is RETRACTED. Rolling arrivals rebound at 0.65 +- 0.03, close to the TP B.6 rolling-arrival anchor ~0.7 that params.rs already cites; whether the engine reproduces 0.65 for rolling arrivals is a cushion-model (spin-coupling) question, to be checked by simulating this exact protocol, not by lowering e_c.
kernel_context.v1_claim_retracted: v1/v2 'cushion is dead, e 0.60-0.69 across all speeds / kernel default e_c = 0.85 is ~0.2 too high' is RETRACTED: it was a composite of the bake-clock artifact and arrival-spin confounding (results-B-v3.json timebase.x2p5_adjudication.e_distortion)

gaps: e(v) with pure-roll arrival above 0.85 m/s: every shot faster than tier1 arrived still sliding (0.73 m run-up too short); the clean e(v) ladder spans only 0.48-0.85 m/s. Extending it needs follow strikes or a longer run-up.
no pure-roll cushion arrivals above ~1 m/s anywhere in the session: the clean rolling e(v) ladder spans only 0.48-0.98 m/s (B tier1 + c0-slide combined)
cushion restitution above ~1 m/s exists only with sliding/partial-slide arrivals (B tier2/3) or unmeasured spin (A fast cells)
A-set and C-set absolute spin decomposition unavailable (A: omega unmeasured; C: |omega| only, +-20% systematic, sign from slate)
